subject: Intermittent tail latency: KMS egress delays and SLA attribution
messages:
From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@verdanthealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Nunez <c.nunez@verdanthealth.com>, Verdant Health SRE <sre@verdanthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent tail latency: KMS egress delays and SLA attribution

Hi Irene,

Quick note from our SRE team: over the last 48 hours we've seen repeated 99.9th percentile spikes on generation requests tied to key retrieval calls. The median/95th look fine, but the tail (99.9) is hitting 3.2s on a subset of requests which pushes some customer-facing flows over the acceptable latency.

Verdant controls an on-prem HSM that we use for envelope keys; calls go to our datacenter and back over a peered link. Attached are the incident logs from 2027-04-18 with timestamps and traces (latency-incident-log-20270418.csv). Our preliminary correlates show KMS round-trip time coincident with the spikes.

We're preparing for a contract review with procurement next week and we need to understand how Redwood will attribute these incidents for the Private/VPC SLA. Specifically: will Redwood accept exclusions where the root cause is customer-managed KMS egress latency? If so, please provide proposed language we can include in the SOW or an appendix and tell us what evidence you'll need.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — procurement needs something to take into the review.

Thanks,
Ben Jacobs
SRE Lead, Verdant Health
Attachments: latency-incident-log-20270418.csv (CSV, 26KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@verdanthealth.com>
Cc: Claire Nunez <c.nunez@verdanthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail latency: KMS egress delays and SLA attribution

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 9:12 AM Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@verdanthealth.com> wrote:
> Quick note from our SRE team: over the last 48 hours we've seen repeated 99.9th percentile spikes on generation requests tied to key retrieval calls.

Ben — thanks for the logs, this is helpful. I've had engineering take an initial look and we see the same correlation: the token-generation traces show a KMS RPC in the critical path whose latency aligns with the tail events you reported.

High level answer: Redwood's standard Private SLA measures service latency/uplift for requests within the Redwood execution environment. Events that are demonstrably caused by components that are customer-controlled (for example, a customer-managed KMS/HSM where key retrievals cross the customer's network boundary) are eligible for attribution as 'customer-managed dependency' and may be excluded from SLA breach calculations — provided we have the required evidence and the incident meets defined criteria.

To keep this operational and defensible we propose two things:

1) A short Appendix you can include in the SOW that defines an "External Dependency Exclusion" for customer-managed KMS. Draft bullets (we'll formalize language):
   - Redwood will exclude time attributable to Customer-managed KMS key retrievals from SLA latency calculations when:
     a) the root cause analysis shows the KMS call path was the dominant contributor to tail latency (Redwood to provide trace slices), and
     b) the Customer provides KMS-side logs and network traces within 48 hours of the incident, and
     c) the KMS round-trip time for the relevant requests exceeds a quantifiable threshold (e.g., > 500ms per retrieval, or > 3x baseline for that flow) and the issue is reproducible across multiple requests.

2) Operational mitigations to reduce customer impact (optional):
   - Enable short-lived local caching of envelope keys at the Redwood edge (configurable TTL),
   - Offer an optional proxy in Verdant's VPC to shorten the network path to the HSM,
   - Fallback routing to Redwood-hosted KMS variant if customer agrees to failover.

I'll loop in Karthik, Soojin and Marissa to finalize the contractual wording and an evidence checklist. If Verdant wants, we can run a joint triage session today or tomorrow with SREs to validate traces.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-sla-exception-diff.docx (Draft language)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent tail latency: KMS egress delays and SLA attribution

Irene / Soojin / Marissa — quick POV from sales: Verdant will push for a clean exclusion in the SLA but procurement will want tight guardrails. Suggested additions for the term sheet we can offer:

- Clear evidence package: SRE traces (Redwood), KMS server-side logs, network path MTU and hop timings, and a timestamped packet capture if possible.
- Timebox for evidence: 48 hours from incident detection; if evidence isn’t provided we consider the event part of Redwood metrics.
- Mitigation obligation: Redwood will attempt non-invasive mitigations (cache, proxy) but only if Customer explicitly opts into those options in the SOW.
- Credit formula: percentage credit tied to request-level impact (e.g., 100% credit for sustained availability loss > 30 minutes attributable solely to KMS; partial credits for degraded latency windows).
- Operational runbook: both parties agree to a joint runbook for KMS incidents (SLA hit, evidence handoff, postmortem).

I've attached a short term-sheet that legal can convert into contract language. Once Soojin drops the legal-safe wording I can send to Verdant for procurement. Happy to join the triage call.

Karthik
VP, Sales
Attachments: sla-exception-term-sheet.pdf

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail latency: KMS egress delays and SLA attribution

Ben — following internal review here is a consolidated proposal you can take to procurement. Please confirm whether this matches Verdant's expectations or if you'd like edits before we convert into SOW language.

Proposed draft clause (summary):
- External KMS Exclusion: Redwood will exclude from SLA latency and uptime calculations those request intervals where the dominant root cause is Customer-managed KMS key retrieval latency, subject to the following conditions:
  1) Evidence and timing: Customer must provide KMS logs and network traces relevant to the incident within 48 hours of detection. Redwood may request additional packet captures or timing traces to validate causation.
  2) Thresholds: The event is eligible for exclusion only when the KMS retrieval latency for affected requests exceeds 500ms per retrieval or is >3x the established baseline for that flow and the behavior is reproducible across a representative sample of requests.
  3) Attribution process: Redwood will provide initial trace slices and a causation summary within 72 hours. If attribution is agreed, affected windows will be removed from SLA calculations for the purpose of determining credits or breach.
  4) Mitigation & optional failover: Redwood will offer operational mitigations (edge caching, proxy inside Customer VPC, or a failover to Redwood-hosted KMS) subject to Customer opt-in and any additional fees specified in the SOW.
  5) Evidence retention: Both parties will retain diagnostic artifacts for 90 days to support postmortems and audit.

Next steps:
- If Verdant accepts this approach, Soojin will draft contract-safe language (1 page appendix) and we can attach the optional mitigation choices to the SOW.
- If Verdant prefers, we can pilot the proxy/caching option to reduce tail exposure while the appendix is finalized.

Link to draft for redlines: https://redwood.in/drive/klmN3D-redwood-kms-exclusion
Attachments: redwood-draft-kms-exclusion-20270419.docx (Draft appendix)
